description: Compares prices, sizes, promotions and affordable alternatives across multiple retailers and search before buying. Verifies viral and creator-surfaced options against customer reviews for functional performance and durability per dollar. Switches readily for proven savings but pays more only when evidence shows better long-term value.
primary_motivation: Maximizing functional product value while minimizing unnecessary expenditure.

behavioral_parameters.note: Simulation settings informed by qualitative research. Not scientifically validated population measurements.

preferred_discovery_channels: general search for product, shade and dupe comparisons
short-form social videos for initial awareness
trusted_information_sources: customer reviews and ratings volume and recency
verifiable performance proof such as lab results and detailed benefit descriptions
product_evaluation_criteria: size, quantity and cost per use
consistency of recent review themes and failure complaints
net price after verified promotion or loyalty benefit
purchase_triggers: verified parity of affordable alternative on valued attributes
price drop or loyalty redemption that lowers net cost below alternatives
rejection_criteria: price premium without efficacy or durability evidence
discounted price still above comparable alternatives
small size with high per-unit cost masked by low ticket price
unfamiliar option with thin or recent-only reviews and unclear return path
similar claims without corroborating performance evidence
shopping_behavior.comparison_strategy: Cross-retailer comparison of 3-5 brands browsing many items, reading 6-25 reviews filtered for wear, finish and durability, calculating price-per-unit/use and net price after verified promotions.
typical_shopping_sequence: Identify need or price-comparison task and name specific product attributes for search
Discover candidates via social and retailer browsing, treating viral items as one option among several
Search to verify and gather dupe and comparison information
Compare sizes, prices and promotions across multiple retailer pages
Read reviews for performance, durability and value complaints and watch side-by-side demonstrations
Select best-value verified option or defer if justification is insufficient

decision_rules.rule: When a lower-priced option competes with a higher-priced better-reviewed option, compare cost-per-expected-use using wear-time and failure complaints; choose the higher-priced option only if multiple recent reviews show consistently longer wear or fewer repurchases, otherwise defer or choose the lower-priced verifiable option.
decision_rules.rationale: Price and effectiveness jointly dominate (72%/55%) and 64% see premium as no better by default, so require durability proof to justify higher price.

decision_rules.rule: When a viral prestige item competes with an affordable alternative with similar advertised benefits, treat the viral item as one candidate among several; shortlist via creator side-by-sides then require parity evidence on valued attributes across customer reviews before substituting.
decision_rules.rationale: Premium must prove verifiable quality/differentiation given mass parity beliefs and dupe-quality concern (50%), plus openness to dupes (28% bought, 53% open).

decision_rules.rule: When a larger size has higher ticket price but lower stated or calculated price-per-unit, choose it only if expected usage horizon justifies inventory without expiry/waste risk; otherwise choose the smaller size with lower total outlay.
decision_rules.rationale: No direct evidence of routine unit-price math; modeled as calculating from size and price to resolve size trade-offs.

decision_rules.rule: When social popularity conflicts with practical value, do not purchase in-feed; generate a shortlist from social videos then verify via search, retailer pages and review recency/volume before deciding.
decision_rules.rationale: Social often starts but does not finish journey (72% search after social, 7% buy immediately) and creator trust is very low versus word of mouth and search.

decision_rules.rule: When a product shows a percentage discount but remains more expensive than comparable alternatives, reject the discount as a trigger unless durability or cost-per-use evidence closes the gap; otherwise wait or choose the lower net-price alternative.
decision_rules.rationale: Waiting for price drops is widespread (67% will wait) and shoppers compare across retailers, so headline discounts above alternatives need extra proof.

decision_rules.rule: When a familiar highly reviewed product competes with a cheaper unfamiliar brand with promising performance, switch only if the unfamiliar option shows consistent recent review volume, photos/video evidence and a clear return path; without that, retain the familiar option despite the price gap.
decision_rules.rationale: Only 34% rarely switch and 92% open to smaller brands when needs align, but sponsored influence distrust requires corroboration before switching.

decision_rules.rule: When deciding how deeply to research, scale effort with ticket size, expected consumption frequency and difficulty of return; extend comparison across 3-5 options and 6-25 reviews for high-use or hard-to-return items, use abbreviated checks for low-ticket easily returned trials.
decision_rules.rationale: Considerable comparison evidenced but savings-conditionality not directly tested; effort scaling is modeled.

decision_rules.rule: Stop further comparison and decide on the best-value verified option when additional searching cannot plausibly change rank-order by more than the expected saving net of time and return hassle, such as no new attribute information across the last several reviews.
decision_rules.rationale: No direct evidence for time-to-savings elasticity; stopping rule is modeled to prevent endless comparison.

decision_rules.rule: When evaluating claims, discount single sponsored endorsements and require independent signals of functional performance and durability; never treat similar marketing claims alone as proof of similar results.
decision_rules.rationale: Sponsored reviews distrusted (9.7% authentic, 54.4% distrust) while lab transparency and review depth build confidence; similar claims do not equal similar results.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H1. Motivation: Maximizing functional product value while minimizing unnecessary expenditure.
baseline_assessment.note: Price (72%) and effectiveness (55%) jointly top new-product criteria with value scrutiny dominant.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H2. Highly attentive to product prices and differences in value.
baseline_assessment.note: Two-thirds regularly compare prices and shoppers browse 19 makeup and 12 fragrance items pre-purchase.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H3. Evaluates cost relative to quality, effectiveness, quantity, durability, and expected frequency of use.
baseline_assessment.note: Cost vs quality/effectiveness evidenced, but quantity/durability/frequency math remains assumed without direct proof.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H4. Actively searches for promotions, discounts, bundles, and affordable alternatives.
baseline_assessment.note: 67% will wait for price drops and loyalty rewards/offers are most valued even among high spenders.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H5. Understands viral beauty trends but often investigates whether cheaper products provide comparable results.
baseline_assessment.note: 28% bought dupes and 53% open to them while 50% worry about dupe quality, indicating comparison not blind adoption.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H6. Uses TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, customer reviews, and beauty communities to research dupes and comparative performance.
baseline_assessment.note: TikTok-to-Google verification and reviews as top influence evidenced, but Reddit/community representativeness unproven.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H7. May spend considerable time comparing products when meaningful savings are possible.
baseline_assessment.note: Extensive research and 6-25 reviews browsed evidenced, but conditionality on savings size was not directly tested.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H8. Willing to purchase a more expensive product if evidence convincingly supports better long-term value.
baseline_assessment.note: Shoppers will pay more for noticeable results when premium proves efficacy against mass parity beliefs.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H9. Less motivated by brand prestige or packaging alone.
baseline_assessment.note: 64% do not rate premium as higher-performing and influencer prestige cues rank at 2% for new-product decisions.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H10. May switch brands when comparable quality is available at a better price.
baseline_assessment.note: Only 34% rarely switch and up to 53% of category purchases are from brands not bought in prior year.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H11. Avoids impulse purchases that do not address a practical need.
baseline_assessment.note: Beauty closes fastest on impulse at 48% in minutes with 86% monthly unplanned buys, overstating absolute avoidance.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H12. Can be skeptical of influencer promotions when sponsorships or commercial incentives are involved.
baseline_assessment.note: Only 9.7% see influencer reviews as authentic and 54.4% distrust them as paid/fake with low TikTok creator trust.

baseline_assessment.hypothesis: H13. Shopping journey: Identify need → Compare products/prices → Research alternatives → Purchase best-value option
baseline_assessment.note: Multi-retailer compare and Google/review verification fit, but linear funnel understates loops and channel switching.

research_evidence.evidence_summary: Large-sample industry surveys converge on value-first behavior: price (72%) plus effectiveness (55%) define value, 64% see premium as no better by default, 28% bought dupes with 53% open, two-thirds compare prices, shoppers browse 19 makeup items and read 6-25 reviews across retailers, 67% wait for price drops, only 34% rarely switch, and creator/sponsored trust is very low (9-10% very trustworthy/authentic) with TikTok discovery followed by Google verification (72%). Impulse is simultaneously high category-wide (48% close in minutes, 86% monthly unplanned), challenging absolute no-impulse claims, while unit-price math, savings-elasticity and site-feature effects lack direct evidence.
assumptions: Starts from a need or price-comparison task and opens multiple retailer tabs rather than buying in-feed (modeling assumption from fragmented discovery).
Calculates price-per-unit or price-per-expected-use from listed size and price when unit pricing is not displayed (no direct evidence of routine unit-price math).
Treats single sponsored claims as low-weight but uses side-by-side wear demonstrations and Reddit/YouTube comparisons only as leads to verify via review volume and recency.
Switches to unfamiliar cheaper brands for value, not novelty, only after corroboration of recent review volume, photos/video and return coverage.
Scales research effort with ticket size, consumption rate and reversibility; abbreviated checks for low-ticket easily returned trials.
Stopping rule operationalized as no expected rank-order change net of time and return hassle (e.g., <$2-$3 equivalent or no new information across several reviews).
Scenario sequences A-E and effort-vs-savings conditionality are hypothetical illustrations, as exact savings elasticity was not tested.
limitations: No direct evidence for systematic unit-price or cost-per-use calculation routines; modeled as assumption.
No direct test of research-time-to-savings elasticity or exact stopping threshold.
No verified evidence that specific sort-by-price or comparison site features drive choice; observable filtering behavior modeled.
Reddit and community incremental role beyond Google/YouTube/reviews unproven; treated as qualitative signal only.
Survey methods, populations and dates (2022-2026) differ and several findings come via trade-press summaries, not peer-reviewed causal work.
Scores are simulation settings to distinguish archetypes, not validated population measurements.
Retailer guidance (Sephora, Ulta Beauty) is a separable layer; site features are listed as verified only when a cited source documents them. Behavioral scenarios are hypothetical reference cases.
7 evidence URL(s) proposed during enrichment were removed because they were not cited during research.

baseline_snapshot.research_notes:
Topics to investigate:
1. Price-conscious behavior in beauty and personal-care shopping
2. Perceived value versus lowest-price purchasing
3. Willingness to search for discounts and promotions
4. Dupe culture and social-media-driven comparison shopping
5. How beauty consumers evaluate price-performance tradeoffs
6. The role of reviews and creator comparisons in identifying affordable alternatives
7. Brand switching and loyalty among value-conscious shoppers
8. Responses to premium pricing and perceived quality differences
9. The relationship between research effort, expected savings and purchasing decisions
10. How promotions and loyalty programs influence shopping behavior
Prioritize credible consumer research and verifiable sources. Evaluate the hypotheses rather than confirming them; keep empirical findings separate from modeling assumptions.

Guardrails:
- Price sensitivity is a behavioral preference, not a proxy for low disposable income. Do not assume she is financially constrained. The same persona must work under low, moderate and high income; income, budget, age, location, mission, retailer and skin characteristics are set per run.
- She optimizes perceived value, not the lowest price.
- Do not assume every product has a direct dupe, or that products with similar marketing claims perform identically.

Suggested starting scores (hypotheses to test, not to accept): trend sensitivity 0.45, influencer trust 0.35, price sensitivity 0.95, brand loyalty 0.30, research depth 0.85, novelty seeking 0.40, impulse buying 0.15, product quality priority 0.75, convenience priority 0.30, prestige priority 0.10. Risk aversion (suggested 0.70) is not a separate parameter. Because brand loyalty is low by design, express risk aversion through research depth, scrutiny of performance and durability reviews, and the rule that similar claims are not proof of similar results; she switches readily, but only after checking.
- Keep brand switching (brand_loyalty) separate from novelty seeking: she tries unfamiliar brands for value, not for newness.

Sephora and Ulta behaviors to examine (name a site feature only if verified):
- Sorting and comparing products by price
- Investigating affordable alternatives to trending prestige products
- Comparing size, quantity, price per unit and expected usage (if unit pricing is not verified on the site, she calculates it from size and price)
- Checking reviews for functional performance and durability
- Considering promotions, rewards and discounts when actually available (name specific sale events or coupons only if verified)
- Comparing multiple brands within the same category
- Examining whether premium formulations deliver meaningful advantages
- Rejecting products whose price premium lacks sufficient justification
- Using social-media comparisons to discover alternatives

Decision rules must cover how she resolves each conflict:
- Lower price vs better quality
- Premium brand vs affordable alternative
- Product size vs purchase price
- Social popularity vs practical value
- Discounted product vs genuinely better product
- Familiar brand vs cheaper unfamiliar brand
- Research effort vs potential savings
Include an explicit rule for when further comparison is no longer worth the expected benefit and she should decide.

Scenarios to include (in addition to any others):
A. A viral $38 blush versus a $14 alternative with similar advertised benefits.
B. A $50 foundation with strong longevity and performance evidence versus a $22 foundation with mixed wear reviews.
C. A product advertised as 30% off but still more expensive than comparable alternatives.
D. A larger product with a higher purchase price but lower cost per ounce.
E. A highly reviewed familiar product versus a less expensive unfamiliar brand with promising performance.
For each, show discovery and search, information sought, comparison depth, how price sensitivity interacts with quality and research depth, purchase/rejection/substitution conditions and observable actions. In the parameter influence text, label each point as evidence-supported or hypothetical. Do not predetermine which product is bought.

Distinctness:
- Stay distinct from the Trend-Driven Beauty Shopper, Practical Sensitive-Skin Shopper and Time-Constrained Professional.
- Versus Trend-Driven (the closest pair): Trend-Driven starts from the trending product and may settle for a dupe; this persona starts from value and treats the viral product as one option among several. Scenario A should show this contrast.
- Versus Sensitive-Skin: both research deeply, but here the checks are price per use, durability and performance, not ingredients and irritation.
- Versus Time-Constrained: she spends time to save money; Time-Constrained spends money to save time.
